Patient note:
A 36-year-old man employed as an urban bicycle courier presented to the ambulatory medicine unit this morning at the request of hematology for a comprehensive medical review before initiating a planned maintenance cycle of obinutuzumab for indolent stage II follicular lymphoid neoplasia that was first discovered fourteen months ago during evaluation of painless cervical and inguinal nodal enlargement; at that time excisional biopsy confirmed a germinal-center phenotype, bone-marrow aspirate was negative for infiltration, and positron–emission tomography demonstrated fluorodeoxyglucose uptake confined to nodal basins above and below the diaphragm without splenic involvement or extranodal masses. He completed six cycles of bendamustine with antibody therapy nine months ago, achieved radiographic disappearance of index nodes, and has remained transfusion-independent with a last complete blood count two weeks ago showing hemoglobin 14.3 g/dL, platelets 288 × 10⁹/L, and neutrophils 3.6 × 10⁹/L. He rode his single-speed bike the three kilometers to clinic, secured it to the rack, and appeared comfortable, remarking only on occasional exertional wheeze when pedaling up the steep hill leading to the campus. Respiratory history reveals childhood asthma that persisted into adulthood: baseline spirometry six months earlier recorded an FEV₁ of 68 % predicted with an FEV₁/FVC ratio of 0.63 and 14 % reversibility after inhaled salbutamol. He inhales budesonide–formoterol 160/4.5 µg twice daily, uses montelukast 10 mg nightly during pollen season, and empties a 200-dose albuterol canister roughly every eight weeks; he has never required intubation, non-invasive ventilation, or systemic steroids beyond short five-day bursts during winter viral infections, and oxygen saturation in clinic today is 97 % breathing ambient air. He denies chronic cough productive of purulent sputum, purplish oral ulcers, or prior pulmonary function tests suggestive of fixed obstruction unrelated to asthma, and plain chest radiograph three months ago showed clear parenchyma and normal cardiac size. Cardiovascular review is equally reassuring: he delivers food orders up four flights without chest tightness, diaphoresis, palpitations, orthopnea, or pedal swelling, and a resting transthoracic echocardiogram obtained last year for chemotherapy baseline documented normal chamber dimensions, an ejection fraction of 64 %, and no valvular pathology. He has never been told of a heart attack, myocarditis, or dilated cardiomyopathy, has not undergone coronary angiography, and his most recent electrocardiogram recorded sinus rhythm at 68 beats/min with a PR interval of 160 ms, QRS 90 ms, and no pathologic Q waves. Lower-extremity endurance is high—he completed a 10-kilometer charity run in 55 minutes last spring—without calf cramps, rest pain, or non-healing blisters, and pedal pulses were bounding during that pre-race physical. Neurologic history is non-contributory: no sudden unilateral weakness, facial droop, speech disturbance, diplopia, seizure, or memory lapses, and he manages online dispatch schedules and personal finances without errors. For hepatic assessment, his hepatologist follows mild steatotic changes attributed to a combination of high-calorie recovery shakes used during amateur power-lifting in his twenties and moderate craft-beer consumption on weekends; ultrasound completed six weeks ago revealed homogeneous hyperechogenicity, smooth contour, and a spleen measuring 11 cm, with portal flow direction preserved, while laboratory tests on the same day showed alanine aminotransferase 58 U/L, aspartate aminotransferase 61 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 82 U/L, total bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL, albumin 4.1 g/dL, and an international normalized ratio of 1.0. He has never experienced jaundice, pruritus, abdominal distention, encephalopathy, hematemesis, or melena, has not required diuretics or endoscopic variceal screening, and maintains a protein-rich Mediterranean diet he prepared under dietitian guidance. Metabolic review identifies no diagnosis of elevated blood sugar; fasting glucose taken with the most recent labs was 97 mg/dL and hemoglobin A1c 5.4 %, and he reports no polyuria, polydipsia, neuropathic symptoms, or retinal issues, though he avoids sugar-sweetened beverages and monitors carbohydrate intake due to a family history of type 2 diabetes in his father. Serum creatinine is 0.9 mg/dL, giving an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 110 mL/min/1.73 m²; blood urea nitrogen is 12 mg/dL, sodium 139 mmol/L, potassium 4.2 mmol/L, chloride 102 mmol/L, and bicarbonate 25 mmol/L, indicating preserved renal acid-base handling. There is no personal history of stomach ulceration, gastrointestinal bleeding, connective-tissue rashes, photosensitivity, or chronic prednisone use. He tested negative for human immunodeficiency virus on three separate occasions over the past five years while donating blood; vaccinations are current for pneumococcus (both conjugate and polysaccharide), hepatitis B, seasonal influenza, and tetanus. He never smoked cigarettes or used vaping devices, denies illicit drug use, and limits alcohol to two pints of beer on Friday evenings. Family history includes a mother alive at 62 with hypothyroidism and a paternal uncle who died of traumatic injury; no first-degree relative suffered premature coronary artery disease, stroke, peripheral bypass, or cirrhotic complications. Current medications are budesonide–formoterol, montelukast, albuterol as needed, cetirizine 10 mg each night for allergic rhinitis, a daily men’s multivitamin, and as-needed ibuprofen for post-ride muscle aches; he reports hives after codeine administration in childhood and therefore avoids opioids. Vital signs today read: temperature 36.6 °C; blood pressure 118/72 mm Hg seated in the right arm; pulse 74 beats/min regular; respiratory rate 14 breaths/min; body-mass index 24 kg/m². He is lean, well-muscled, and speaks in full sentences without accessory-muscle use. Carotid upstrokes are brisk without bruit, jugular venous pressure is estimated at 3 cm above the sternal angle, the point of maximal impulse is palpable in the fifth intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line, heart sounds are crisp with no extra gallops or murmurs, lungs are clear to auscultation aside from faint end-expiratory wheeze over the right upper lobe, abdomen is flat and nontender with a smooth liver edge palpable 1 cm below the costal margin, and there is no splenomegaly or ascites. Extremities are warm with 2+ radial, posterior tibial, and dorsalis pedis pulses, capillary refill under two seconds, no cyanosis, clubbing, or edema. Neurologic screen displays alert affect, orientation to person, place, and date, intact cranial nerves II through XII, 5/5 strength throughout, symmetric reflexes, normal vibration and light-touch sensation distally, rapid alternating movements intact, heel-to-shin smooth, and a narrow-based gait. He requests confirmation that his airways are sufficiently controlled for the forthcoming antibody infusion, guidance on liver-friendly nutritional adjustments, and reassurance that cycling to work remains safe given his current hematologic status.

Question: What is the patient's Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) sums weights for qualifying chronic conditions. In the age-adjusted score, age under 50 adds no points.
- Age 36 → 0.
- Chronic pulmonary disease: persistent asthma with airflow obstruction (FEV₁ 68% predicted) requiring daily inhaled therapy → 1.
- Mild liver disease: hepatic steatosis with mild transaminitis, preserved synthetic function, and no evidence of portal hypertension → 1.
- Lymphoma: follicular lymphoma under ongoing hematology care with maintenance therapy planned → 2. It is not counted again as a solid tumor.
- No documented MI, heart failure, peripheral vascular or cerebrovascular disease, dementia, connective tissue disease, peptic ulcer, diabetes, hemiplegia, moderate/severe kidney disease, leukemia, solid tumor, or AIDS → 0 additional points.
Total = 0 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 0 = 4.
Final answer: 4
